audit.whatIsWrong: phases[5].side said Fizz while win[5] said Aurelion Sol, and phases[6].side said Skill while win[6] said Aurelion Sol. The content layer also handed Aurelion Sol the first-item stage outright in a matchup he loses at 45.38% over 877 games.
audit.why: 45.38% is the worst rate in this slice. One completed item does not flip a lane where Playful / Trickster still dodges the only lockdown Aurelion Sol has; the honest chart is Fizz through level 6, even at first item, Aurelion Sol at two items.
audit.corrected: Row 5 set to Skill on both layers, row 6 set to Aurelion Sol on both layers.

audit.whatIsWrong: Chum the Waters was called a guaranteed slow into a full combo, and nothing anywhere stated that Playful / Trickster's landing grounds you or that the untargetable window eats a 120-second Falling Star.
audit.why: Riot's text: the fish is thrown in a direction and attaches to any champion that touches it — it is a 1300-range skillshot that can be sidestepped or eaten by an ally, not a guarantee. The E landing carries a grounding flag, which shuts off Astral Flight, so the escape a player is told to save is not available during the follow-up. And spending R into the untargetable hop costs 120 seconds for nothing.
audit.corrected: Stated in breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, spikes[1], wants.foe[1] and enemyWin, with the 16s rank-1 E cooldown.

notes: The level-chart change here is the one judgement call in my slice: I moved the first-item row from Aurelion Sol to Skill rather than leaving the two layers disagreeing. Rationale is the 45.38% win rate plus the fact that Rod of Ages does not solve the untargetable window. If the user prefers the optimistic read, flipping row 5 to Aurelion Sol on BOTH layers is the alternative and equally consistent — but it must be both. Chum the Waters carries a 'projectile' flag; whether it can be blocked by Wind Wall-class effects is not in Riot's text, so I did not assert it.
